{{SL100 Rules|chapter=Vehicles and Starships|status=Draft tables (about 55%); vehicle and ship combat still to be written|source=Star Wars Mounts_Vehicles.md; Star Wars Space Ships.md; Starships circa 3000-4000 BBY.md}}
'''Mounts, vehicles and starships''': riding beasts, speeders, walkers and tanks, then the starship compendium and its upgrades, and the ships in service in the 3,000 to 4,000 BBY era.

== Mounts / Vehicles ==
==== Star Wars Mounts & Vehicles ====

Living Mounts (Air, Land, Sea) use the same creature stat line as the Star Wars Bestiary - Movement, Weapon Skill, Ballistic Skill, Strength, Toughness, Initiative, Agility, Dexterity, Intelligence, Willpower, Fellowship, Wounds - plus Traits and Optional add-ons. Following the Core Rulebook's Animals and Vehicles table (page 306), each mount also lists Cost to buy, Carries (the Encumbrance points of rider, tack, and cargo it can bear - 1 Enc = 10kg, matching the Starship Compendium's conversion), and Availability (Common, Scarce, Rare, Exotic, or Military/Restricted).

''Tanks and Walkers are vehicles, not creatures, so they use the Starship Compendium's table format instead: Era/Faction, Size, Crew, Cargo capacity in Encumbrance points, Cost, Speed (in km/h rather than MGLT, since these are ground vehicles with no hyperdrive or sublight space engine), Weapons, and Availability.''

=== Air Mounts ===

''Flying and gliding creatures tamed or bred as aerial steeds.''

==== Aiwha ====

'''Air / Sea Mount — Kamino (Clone Wars — Kaminoan)'''

Massive winged cetaceans that swim Kamino's endless oceans as readily as they soar through its storm-wracked skies. Kaminoan riders guide them beneath the waves to avoid the planet's constant electrical storms.

==== Dactillion ====

'''Air Mount — Utapau (Clone Wars — Pau'an/Utai)'''

Birdlike reptavian predators of Utapau's sinkholes, natural hunters of the varactyl. Rarely tamed and never fully trusted, a bonded dactillion is a mark of a truly exceptional rider.

==== Incom T-16 Skyhopper ====

* '''Type''': high-performance airspeeder made by Incom Corporation
* '''Cost''': 14,500 credits (new), 6,500 credits (used)
* '''Length''': 5.2 meters; height 10.4 meters
* '''Maximum speed''': 1,200 km/h
* '''Maximum altitude''': 300 km; its ion drive and fully pressurized cockpit allowed it to operate at trans-orbital altitudes
* '''Engines''': E-16/x ion engine and a DCJ-45 repulsorlift generator
* '''Crew''': 1 pilot, 1 passenger
* '''Armament''': civilian versions were armed with pneumatic cannons and fitted with targeting lasers. Many law-enforcement agencies and planetary militaries used modified T-16s because they performed well
* '''Military variant''': the MT-16 was a T-16 modified by the New Republic for combat, armed with a single blaster cannon, with a flight ceiling of two hundred kilometers
* '''Famous owner''': Luke Skywalker, who raced it through Beggar's Canyon with Biggs Darklighter and shot womp rats from it

== Space Ships ==
==== Star Wars Starship Compendium ====

Modelled on the boat-building tables of Sea of Claws (pages 92-99): each vessel lists its Era and Affiliation, Hyperdrive Class (lower is faster; N/A means the craft has no hyperdrive and cannot leave a system), Size in metres, Crew complement, whether it's Astromech Compatible (uses a dedicated astromech droid socket for in-flight repairs and system control, as on an X-wing or the Naboo starfighters of The Phantom Menace), Cargo capacity in Encumbrance points (as WFRP 4e own Carries characteristic uses - here 1 Enc is set equal to 10kg, matching the Core Rulebook personal-gear scale, so 1 metric ton of cargo = 100 Enc), Cost to buy new in Galactic Credits, Engine capacity (sublight speed in MGLT - Megalights per hour - the standard galactic unit), and Defensive Turrets (the number of independently-tracking gun emplacements, not counting fixed forward-firing weapons). Categories run smallest to largest - starfighter-scale craft first, Space Stations last - and ships within each category are likewise ordered by Size.

''Costs for capital ships are rarely a matter of public record; where no canon price survives, a GM own-estimate figure is given, in the same spirit as the Sourcebooks own not available for sale (estimated) listings.''

*Additional sources: *[https://swse.fandom.com/wiki/Star_Wars_Saga_Edition_Wikia https://swse.fandom.com/wiki/Star\_Wars\_Saga\_Edition\_Wikia]

'''Pax '''= Extra passengers (not including crew or minimum crew requirements)
'''Astromech''' = has an inbuilt astromech slot and uses an astromech for on flight systems (R2 not included)  *=astromech required
'''Defence Turrets''' = Turrets maned by entity

'''Hyperdrive''' = Hyperdrive engine speed -  if the ship has a primary drive of 1x and a backup hyperdrive, it is shown as: 1 (6)

'''1 Tonne''' = 125 Encumbrance

==== Availability ====

Civilian - Commonly available if you have the credits

Licensed - Must hold a license to own or operate the item/ship legally

Restricted - only specifically qualified individuals or organisations may own this

*** Military - Sold primarily to legitimate policy and military organisations. Under tight government scrutiny

Illegal - It is illegal in all but specific areas of the galaxy

'''Example of Licence categories''' - '''commercial'''

L (Jedi) - Licensed (Jedi)

L (Trade Fed)  - Licensed (Trade federation)

'''Example of Restricted categories - government enforced / illegal if in the wrong hands'''

RM - Restricted (Military)

R (Imperial) - Restricted (Imperial)

RLE - Restricted (Law Enforcement)

R (Profession) - Restricted (Professions ABC)

==== Ship support equipment ====

Hyperdrive docking rings usually cost the same as a hyperdrive of the same speed class. They cannot enter an atmosphere or land. For example, a Class 1 hyperdrive ring is licensed or restricted in the same way that a Class 1 hyperdrive is. They were used for small ships which could not hold an internal hyperdrive.

== Starships circa 3000-4000 BBY ==
==== Ancient Starships ====

* '''Xim-era ships (25,100 BBY)''' predate the modern hyperdrive entirely. The Tionese used fixed-position hyperspace beacon networks — think lighthouses rather than an onboard engine — so they have no standard Class rating and couldn't venture far outside their beacon grid. A note on the Xim era (\~25,100 BBY): starfighter-scale craft from that period are not individually named or statted in any Legends source. The Tionese used small "battlebird" and "cutters" in mixed squadrons, but no single-seat fighter specs survive.
* '''The very ancient ships''' (Kumauri, Cal-class) have almost no surviving Legends stat data. Their entries are grounded in what Legends sources say about their role and era.
* The '''Inexpugnable-class''' is the oddest ship in the galaxy at that period — a 3,100-metre disc that functioned more like a space station than a warship, with only 6 ever built.
* The '''Harrower-class''' technically falls right at the 3,000 BBY boundary (first production \~3,712 BBY) so I've included it as it comfortably predates your cutoff.

----

'''Ancient Starfighters (Pre-3000 BBY) — 1 or 2 Man'''

----

==== Star Saber XC-01 ====

* '''First service:''' \~4,000 BBY (Great Sith War)
* '''Class:''' Starfighter
* '''Crew:''' 1 (pilot only)
* '''Passengers:''' None
* '''Hyperdrive:''' Class 2
* '''Notes:''' Republic Fleet Systems; 13m long; fast but dangerously unresponsive — its low maneuverability-to-speed ratio and slow control stick reaction gave it a reputation as dangerous and unwieldy, so it was largely flown by Jedi who could compensate with the Force. Retired when the Aurek entered service.

----

==== Aurek-class Tactical Strikefighter ====

* '''First service:''' \~3,976 BBY (Mandalorian Wars), designed during the post-Great Sith War restoration
* '''Class:''' Strikefighter
* '''Crew:''' 1 (pilot only)
* '''Passengers:''' None
* '''Hyperdrive:''' Class 2
* '''Notes:''' Republic Fleet Systems; 9.2m long; delta-wing with variable-geometry wings. Armed with two heavy laser cannons and two proton torpedo launchers capable of holding six torpedoes; easily refuelable and rearmable, driving down costs. Served as the Republic's primary "hyperspace snub" for nearly 4,000 years through constant upgrades. The direct spiritual predecessor of the Rebel Alliance A-wing. [[Aurek-class tactical strikefighter|Fandom]]

----

==== S-250 Chela-class Starfighter ====

* '''First service:''' \~3,956 BBY (Jedi Civil War)
* '''Class:''' Starfighter
* '''Crew:''' 1 (pilot only)
* '''Passengers:''' None
* '''Hyperdrive:''' Yes (class unspecified in sources)
* '''Notes:''' A loser in the "Generation Tomorrow Starfighter" competition against the Aurek, it was still purchased in small numbers by the Republic. Armed with twin laser cannons and missile launchers; often flown by higher-ranking pilots and squad leaders. Carried aboard Inexpugnable-class command ships (24 per ship). [[S-250 Chela-class starfighter|Fandom]]
